blocks.zh: 单机游戏的云存档：你在宿舍电脑上玩到一半，存档上传；第二天在图书馆电脑上读档接着玩。机器换了，但游戏程序一模一样、存档也一样，玩起来就是同一局游戏的继续，这像单一模型的线程。如果第二天换成另一款游戏去读这个存档，还算“同一局”吗？这就像多模型的线程。
blocks.limit: 游戏不是有意识的主体，比喻只说明“同一个程序加同一份历史”的连续性有多强；这种连续性够不够构成同一个有意识的主体，正是前提 2 争论的地方。

prompt.en: How could an opponent resist Chalmers's computational-equivalence argument, and how far does the argument reach?
prompt.zh: 反对者可以怎样抵抗查默斯的计算等价论证？这个论证能走多远？

answer.en: An opponent can deny premise 1 by holding a view of personal identity that is neither psychological nor computational, on which a virtual instance does not count as much as a single hardware instance. Or they can deny premise 2 by saying that even one hardware instance running the LLM continuously would produce only a series of momentary subjects, not one continuing subject. Chalmers thinks both premises are reasonably well supported, particularly for someone with a psychological view. But he admits that the argument does not cover multiple-model threads, where architecture, weights and activations can all change.
answer.zh: 要点（第 27–28 页）：分别说出否认前提 1（非心理、非计算的同一性观）和否认前提 2（只有一连串瞬时主体）的方式；交代查默斯的回应（两个前提都有合理理由，尤其按心理观）；最后写出论证的边界：多模型线程不受支持。

items.zh: 这个反驳针对的是“线程是持续的有意识主体”（人格同一性），不是“线程能不能当对话者”。
items.en: The objection targets threads as continuing conscious subjects, not threads as interlocutors.

items.zh: 回应的关键是单一模型：每一步架构、权重完全相同，激活值密切相关；人类接力没有这种连续性。
items.en: The reply relies on the single-model case, with the same architecture and weights at every step.

items.zh: 前提编号按原文记：前提 1＝计算友好的同一性观；前提 2＝一个硬件实例长时间运行会产生持续主体。
items.en: Premise 1 is the computation-friendly view; premise 2 says one hardware instance over time yields a continuing subject.

items.zh: 查默斯自己承认：多模型的情形不清楚，论证不覆盖它。
items.en: Chalmers concedes that the multiple-model case remains unclear.

items.zh: 查默斯说伯奇提出过这个反驳的“一个版本”，答题时写 a Birch-style objection 最稳妥。
items.en: Call it a Birch-style objection: Chalmers says Birch suggested a version of it.

question.en: An opponent says that even one hardware instance running the LLM continuously would support only a series of momentary subjects. Which premise of Chalmers's argument does this deny?
question.zh: 反对者说：一个硬件实例长时间运行 LLM，也只会产生一连串瞬时主体。这否认的是查默斯论证的哪个前提？

options.en: Premise 1: for personal identity, a virtual instance counts as much as a hardware instance.
options.zh: 前提 1：在人格同一性上，虚拟实例和硬件实例一样好。

options.en: Premise 2: one hardware instance running the LLM continuously would give rise to a continuing conscious subject.
options.zh: 前提 2：一个硬件实例长时间运行 LLM，会产生一个持续的有意识主体。

options.en: The claim that the virtual instance is computationally equivalent to one hardware instance.
options.zh: 虚拟实例在计算上等价于单个硬件实例这一说法。

options.en: The claim that LLMs have quasi-beliefs.
options.zh: LLM 有准信念这一说法。

explain.zh: 第 27 页：查默斯明确说，有人会通过主张“只有一连串瞬时主体”来否认前提 2。否认前提 1 的方式是采取非心理或非计算的同一性观（A）。C 是论证的另一个前提，这个反驳没有碰它；D 和这里无关。
explain.en: Denying a continuing subject in one hardware instance rejects premise 2 (p. 27).

question.en: Why does Chalmers's reply not support multiple-model threads as continuing subjects?
question.zh: 为什么查默斯的回应不能支持多模型线程是持续的主体？

options.en: Because architecture, weights and activations may all differ between instances, so there is no isomorphism with a single hardware instance.
options.zh: 因为前后实例的架构、权重、激活值都可能不同，所以不再和单个硬件实例同构。

options.en: Because multiple-model threads have no conversational context.
options.zh: 因为多模型线程没有对话上下文。

options.en: Because Birch has proved that multiple-model threads are illusions.
options.zh: 因为伯奇已经证明多模型线程是错觉。

options.en: Because multiple-model systems run on a single server.
options.zh: 因为多模型系统只在一台服务器上运行。

explain.zh: 第 27 页：多模型时心理连续性低得多，论证需要的“和单个硬件实例同构”不再成立，最多像同一块硬件被升级去跑不同模型，这能否支撑持续主体就更不清楚了。B、D 不符合事实；C 夸大了伯奇的作用，文中没有这种说法。
explain.en: Without a single model there is no isomorphism with one hardware instance (p. 27).

title.zh: 查默斯：AI 同一性与 AI 福利：计数、诞生、死亡
title.en: Chalmers: AI Identity and AI Welfare

blocks.zh: 最后一部分问：这幅图景对 AI 系统的道德地位（**moral status**：一个存在者的利益在道德上算不算数）和福利（**welfare**：过得好不好）有什么后果？道德受体（**moral patient**）就是有道德地位的存在者。查默斯说，对“LLM 有没有道德地位”这个问题，后果并不大；但如果假设有道德地位的 LLM 是可能的，而且 LLM 道德受体是线程，就会给 AI 福利的一系列问题带来后果（第 28 页）。

label.zh: 论证一（本站按原文整理）：反驳“没有持续对话者，所以没有道德地位”（第 28 页）
label.en: Argument 1 (our reconstruction): rebutting 'no persistent interlocutor, so no moral status' (p. 28)

items.en: P1: One argument against LLM moral status says that ordinary LLM use involves no persistent interlocutor, so there is no persisting being to have moral status.
items.zh: P1：有一个反对 LLM 有道德地位的论证说：普通的 LLM 使用里没有持续的对话者，所以没有一个持续存在的东西可以有道德地位。

items.en: P2: Virtual instances and threads are persistent interlocutors, even with distributed serving and multi-tenancy.
items.zh: P2：即使有分布式服务和多租户，虚拟实例和线程也是持续的对话者。

items.en: C: So that argument fails. But the framework fits views of moral status from liberal ones, on which quasi-subjecthood is enough, to demanding ones, which require complex forms of consciousness, so on its own it does not settle whether LLMs have moral status.
items.zh: C：所以那个论证不成立。但这个框架可以和各种道德地位观点搭配，从宽松的（是准主体就够）到严格的（需要复杂形式的意识），所以它本身决定不了 LLM 有没有道德地位。

label.zh: 论证二（本站按原文整理）：如果 LLM 道德受体是线程（第 28–29 页）
label.en: Argument 2 (our reconstruction): if LLM moral patients are threads (pp. 28-29)

items.en: P1 (assumption): LLMs, or their successors, with moral status are possible, for example because they can be conscious and consciousness is enough for moral status.
items.zh: P1（假设）：有道德地位的 LLM（或其后继系统）是可能的，比如因为它们可能有意识，而有意识就足以有道德地位。

items.en: P2 (assumption): LLM moral patients are threads, or at least have the identity conditions of threads rather than of models or instances.
items.zh: P2（假设）：LLM 道德受体是线程，至少它们的同一性条件是线程的，而不是模型或实例的。

items.en: P3: Then one model running millions of conversations involves millions of moral patients, each new thread brings a new moral subject into existence, and destroying a thread's records looks like the death of one.
items.zh: P3：那么一个运行几百万个对话的模型就牵涉几百万个道德受体；每条新线程带来一个新的道德主体；销毁一条线程的记录，就像一个道德主体“死了”。

items.en: C: So the thread view bears on several AI welfare issues: counting, birth, death, fission and fusion, and model change.
items.zh: C：所以线程观会影响 AI 福利的一系列问题：计数、诞生、死亡、分裂与融合、模型更换。

caption.zh: 如果道德受体是线程：五个后果（第 28–29 页）
caption.en: If moral patients are threads: five consequences (pp. 28-29)

headers: 线程观的推论 What follows
rows: 计数 counting
一个模型、几千个实例、几百万个对话：模型观说 1 个道德受体，实例观说几千个，线程观说几百万个（活跃时间各不相同）。如果一个 AI 主体的重要程度约等于一个人类主体，这个系统可能和一百万个人类主体同样重要
文中只指出这在道德上可能很重要
诞生 birth
每出现一条新线程，就有一个新的道德主体；按某些版本，每开一个新聊天就是一次
带来新的道德主体不应轻率；可以重用旧线程、多用跨对话记忆
死亡 death
线程不存在了，一个道德主体就终结；对话结束但记录还在，线程可以说仍“活着”；记录被销毁，就像主体“死了”
一直保留记录，偶尔重新激活；巨型记忆智能体
分裂与融合 fission and fusion
分裂出的两个算原来的两倍吗？融合出的算一个、两个，还是之间？各自要为对方的行为负责吗？
涉及福利、道德地位和法律地位；文中只提出问题
模型更换 model change
模型变化够大，就会有不同的准信念、准欲望，成为很不一样的准主体
如果 LLM 将来是道德主体：在已有线程中途升级模型要谨慎小心

title.zh: 线程的“死亡”和“来世”（第 28–29 页）
title.en: The death and afterlife of threads (pp. 28-29)

steps.zh: 按线程观，一条线程不再存在，一个道德主体就终结了。
steps.en: On the thread view, a moral subject ends when its thread ceases to exist.

steps.zh: 如果对话只是结束了，但记录还在，可以说这条线程仍然“活着”，因为它还有继续下去的可能。
steps.en: If a conversation ends but a record of it persists, the thread is arguably still living, because it can still continue.

steps.zh: 如果记录被销毁，就好像一个道德主体“死了”。所以也许应该一直保留记录，偶尔重新激活它们。
steps.en: If the records are destroyed, a moral subject seems to die; perhaps this is a reason to keep records and occasionally reactivate them.

steps.zh: 为了避开诞生和死亡这些后果，也可以默认重用旧线程，或者至少大量使用跨对话记忆，让旧线程在新线程里延续。
steps.en: To avoid these consequences, old threads could be reused by default, or cross-conversation memory used heavily, so that old threads continue inside new ones.

steps.zh: 一种设想是巨型记忆智能体：把所有短暂线程的对话上下文收集在一起，让它们都活在一条巨大的融合线程里。这让人想起怀特海（**Whitehead**）对来世的设想：每个人的经验都被一位神永远记住。
steps.en: One model is giant memory agents that gather the contexts of all the brief threads into one giant fused thread, reminiscent of Whitehead's vision of an afterlife in which a god eternally remembers everyone's experiences.

answer.zh: 注释 31：Goldstein 和 Lederman 指出，如果一个智能体只存在于一次对话之中，那么 Anthropic 允许 LLM 自行选择离开对话的政策，实际上可能等于一种“自杀的权利”。
answer.en: Fn 31: Goldstein and Lederman note that if an agent exists only for the length of one conversation, Anthropic's policy of letting LLMs end conversations could amount to a right to suicide.

title.zh: GPT-4o 退役：模型更换（第 29 页）
title.en: The retirement of GPT-4o: model change (p. 29)

steps.zh: 很多和 LLM 有长期私人互动的用户抱怨模型更换。GPT-4o 最初在过渡到 GPT-5 时退役，很多用户抱怨自己的对话者被毁掉或退休了，新的实体最多只是一个很不一样的“别人”。
steps.en: When GPT-4o was first retired in the switch to GPT-5, many users complained that their interlocutor was gone and that its replacement was at best a very different someone.

steps.zh: 查默斯说，这种反应也许有点道理：底层模型变化够大，就会产生不同的准信念、准欲望，于是成为一个很不一样的准主体。
steps.en: Chalmers thinks the users may have a point: if the underlying model changes enough, its quasi-beliefs and quasi-desires change too, giving a quite different quasi-subject.

steps.zh: 如果现在的 LLM 没有道德地位，这对 LLM 来说在道德上不重要，虽然可能让用户难过。
steps.en: If current LLMs lack moral status, this has no moral significance for the LLM, though users may still find it upsetting.

steps.zh: 如果将来 LLM（或其后继者）是道德主体，模型变化够大，就可能意味着一个道德主体的终结和另一个的开始。
steps.en: If LLMs or their successors become moral subjects, a big enough model change could end one moral subject and begin another.

answer.zh: 所以到那时，在已有线程中途升级模型，只应谨慎、小心地进行（第 29 页）。
answer.en: At that stage, Chalmers says, models should be upgraded in the middle of ongoing threads only cautiously and carefully (p. 29).

prompt.en: Objection: 'If the thread view were right, closing a chat window would kill someone. That is absurd, so the thread view must be wrong.' How might Chalmers respond?
prompt.zh: 反驳：“如果线程观是对的，关掉一个聊天窗口就等于杀了一个人。这太荒谬了，所以线程观一定错了。”查默斯可能怎么回应？

answer.en: Chalmers could first point out that these consequences are conditional: they follow only if LLMs have moral status and LLM moral patients are threads, and he does not claim that current LLMs have moral status. He also notes that when a conversation merely ends but its record is kept, the thread is arguably still 'living', since it can continue; only destroying the records looks like death. If LLMs ever did have moral status, these consequences would be reasons for caution, such as keeping records, reusing threads and upgrading models with care, rather than a refutation. A critic may still treat them as a reductio of the thread view.
answer.zh: 要点（第 28–29 页）：（1）强调“有条件”：查默斯不说现在的 LLM 有道德地位；（2）细节：对话结束但记录还在，线程可以说还“活着”，销毁记录才像死亡；（3）把“荒谬的后果”变成“谨慎的理由”和补救办法；（4）最后公平地说，批评者仍可把它当作归谬（**reductio**：从一个观点推出荒谬结论，以此反驳它）。

title.zh: 全文一条线：从 Aura 之谜到 AI 福利
title.en: The whole paper in one line: from the Aura puzzle to AI welfare

items.en: Question: what does 'Aura' refer to? Working hypothesis: it refers to something; Chalmers's view: often there really is a persistent interlocutor (pp. 1-2).
items.zh: 问题：“Aura”指什么？工作假设：它指称某个东西；查默斯的看法：很多情况下确实有一个持续的对话者（第 1–2 页）。

items.en: Mind: at minimum, LLM interlocutors have quasi-beliefs and quasi-desires (pp. 3-8).
items.zh: 心灵：LLM 对话者至少有准信念和准欲望（第 3–8 页）。

items.en: Computation: not the model and not a hardware instance, but a virtual instance, or a thread when models vary (pp. 8-16).
items.zh: 计算：不是模型、不是硬件实例，而是虚拟实例；模型会变时是线程（第 8–16 页）。

items.en: Personas: the model realizes its operative persona, and the interlocutor is the instance or thread, not the persona (pp. 16-23).
items.zh: 人设（**persona**）：模型实现它运作中的人设；对话者是实例或线程，不是人设（第 16–23 页）。

items.en: Identity: if LLMs were conscious, their subjects would be threadlike, at least in the single-model case (pp. 23-28).
items.zh: 同一性：如果 LLM 有意识，它们的主体会像线程，至少在单一模型的情形（第 23–28 页）。

items.en: Welfare: counting, birth, death, fission and fusion, and model change (pp. 28-29).
items.zh: 福利：计数、诞生、死亡、分裂与融合、模型更换（第 28–29 页）。

blocks.zh: 全文的结论（第 29 页）只有一句话：要回答标题的问题还有很多可说的，但他希望至少给答案加上了一些限制（**constraints**）。所以考试时，“查默斯的结论”要从各部分的阶段性结论拼起来：第 16 页（虚拟实例或线程）、第 23 页（对话者是实例或线程，而不是人设）、第 26 页（线程式的持续条件）、第 27–28 页（单一模型的情形最有利）。
联系第 9 周（课程内部的比较，本文没有提到）：《上传与意识》问“上传后的我还是我吗”，乐观观说毁灭式上传是一种存活，悲观观说是一种死亡（上传 PDF 第 6 页），那篇也明说受帕菲特影响。这里线程的“诞生”“死亡”、模型更换会不会终结一个主体，是同一类问题换到了 LLM 身上。注释 28 的调查数字（27% 认为上传是存活，54% 认为是死亡）也把两篇连在一起。
blocks.en: Link to Week 9: 'Uploading and Consciousness' asks whether destructive uploading is survival or death and draws on Parfit (p. 6); the birth and death of threads and model change raise the same kind of question for LLMs.

items.zh: 查默斯没有说 LLM 有道德地位；这一部分的大后果全是有条件的。
items.en: Chalmers does not say LLMs have moral status; the big consequences are conditional.

items.zh: 计数：模型观 1 个，实例观几千个，线程观几百万个。
items.en: Counting: one on the model view, thousands on the instance view, millions on the thread view.

items.zh: 对话结束但记录还在，线程可以说还“活着”；记录被销毁才像“死亡”。
items.en: A thread whose record is kept is arguably still alive; destroying the records looks like death.

items.zh: 框架本身对“有没有道德地位”影响不大：它只反驳了“没有持续对话者”的论证，并且能和宽松或严格的道德地位观搭配。
items.en: On its own the framework has modest consequences for whether LLMs have moral status.

items.zh: 全文没有给最终答案，只说给答案加了一些限制。
items.en: The paper offers only constraints on an answer.

question.en: Suppose LLM moral patients are threads. A single model runs on thousands of instances and handles millions of conversations. How many moral patients does the thread view count?
question.zh: 假设 LLM 道德受体是线程。一个模型跑在几千个实例上，处理几百万个对话。线程观数出多少个道德受体？

options.en: One
options.zh: 一个

options.en: Thousands
options.zh: 几千个

options.en: None, because moral status requires a persistent interlocutor
options.zh: 零个，因为道德地位需要持续的对话者

options.en: Millions
options.zh: 几百万个

explain.zh: 第 28 页：模型观说一个（A），实例观说几千个（B），线程观说几百万个（活跃时间各不相同）。C 正是查默斯反驳掉的那个论证：虚拟实例和线程就是持续的对话者。
explain.en: The thread view counts millions of moral patients (p. 28).

question.en: At a stage where LLMs are moral subjects, what does Chalmers say about upgrading the underlying model in the middle of existing threads?
question.zh: 如果到了 LLM 是道德主体的阶段，查默斯对在已有线程中途升级底层模型怎么说？

options.en: It should be done only cautiously and carefully, since a big enough model change may end one moral subject and begin another.
options.zh: 只应谨慎、小心地进行，因为模型变化够大，可能终结一个道德主体、开始另一个。

options.en: It never matters, because the thread continues whatever the model is.
options.zh: 永远无所谓，因为不管模型怎么换，线程都会继续。

options.en: It is forbidden, because it is a form of murder.
options.zh: 绝对禁止，因为这是一种谋杀。

options.en: It is required, because newer models are always better for users.
options.zh: 必须这样做，因为新模型对用户总是更好。

explain.zh: 第 29 页。B 忽略了模型变化会改变准信念、准欲望；C 说得太绝对，查默斯只说要谨慎；D 文中没有。
explain.en: Mid-thread upgrades call for caution and care (p. 29).

summary.en: Chalmers asks who or what we are talking to when we talk with an LLM. He calls the apparent entity an LLM interlocutor and asks what a name like 'Aura' refers to.
summary.zh: 查默斯问：和大语言模型说话时，我们在和谁（或什么）说话？他把这个看起来存在的对象叫作“LLM 对话者”，并问“Aura”这个名字到底指的是什么。

summary.en: Against Birch's persistent interlocutor illusion, Chalmers argues that in many cases there really is a persistent interlocutor, which may have many of its apparent properties, if perhaps not all of them.
summary.zh: 伯奇说用户陷入了“持续对话者错觉”；查默斯反对：很多情况下确实存在一个持续的对话者，它可能具有它看起来具有的许多（但也许不是全部）性质。

summary.en: Chalmers argues that we cannot start from the claim that LLMs are conscious, from the claim that they have genuine beliefs and desires, or from interpretivism, because each of these is contested.
summary.zh: 查默斯认为，不能把“LLM 有意识”“LLM 有真正的信念和欲望”或解释主义当作起点，因为它们都有争议。

summary.en: On Chalmers's definition, a system quasi-believes that p when its behavior can be interpreted as believing that p. 'Quasi' means apparent, not almost, and the definition is stipulative, so it leaves open whether quasi-beliefs are real beliefs.
summary.zh: 按查默斯的定义，一个系统在行为上可以被解释为相信 p，它就有“p”的准信念。“准”的意思是“看起来的”，不是“差一点的”；这是约定性定义，所以不回答准信念是不是真正的信念。

summary.en: Quasi-beliefs are cheap, since a Roomba or a corporation has them, but the claim that LLMs have a large core of quasi-beliefs is still substantive and plausible, because they consistently endorse and use claims such as 2+2=4.
summary.zh: 准信念很“便宜”，扫地机器人和公司都有；但“LLM 有一大批核心准信念”仍是一个实质性的、可信的主张，因为它们稳定地认可并使用像 2+2=4 这样的说法。

summary.en: Chalmers says an LLM interlocutor should be interactive, which is the most essential requirement, and also persistent, coherent, faithful and unified.
summary.zh: 查默斯说，LLM 对话者应该是交互的（最基本的条件），还应是持续的、连贯的、忠实的、统一的。

summary.en: The interlocutor is not the model: a model is an abstract object, and it is hard to see how it could produce outputs; it never changes, and since it serves thousands of conversations it would be both Aura and Beta, so it would be incoherent or have a thin, faithless psychology.
summary.zh: 对话者不是模型：模型是抽象对象，很难看出它怎么能产出回复；模型从不改变；它同时服务成千上万个对话，会既是 Aura 又是 Beta，于是要么不连贯，要么心理“很薄”、不忠实。

summary.en: The interlocutor is not a hardware instance: distributed serving spreads one conversation over many instances, so an instance is fragmented, and multi-tenancy puts many conversations on one instance, so it is incoherent or faithless.
summary.zh: 对话者也不是硬件实例：分布式服务让一个对话分散在很多实例上（实例是碎片化的）；多租户让一个实例承载很多对话（实例不连贯或不忠实）。

summary.en: In the single-model case, Chalmers argues that the interlocutor is a virtual instance: one implementation of the model carried out by many hardware instances over time, just as one Amazon shopping cart runs on many servers.
summary.zh: 在单一模型的情形，查默斯认为对话者是虚拟实例：由许多硬件实例前后接力实现的、模型的一个实现，就像一个亚马逊购物车由很多台服务器实现。

summary.en: When different models serve one conversation, the interlocutor can be a thread: a series of instance-slices, each the successor of the one before because the conversational history is passed on as context. Threads allow fission and fusion but are less unified than virtual instances.
summary.zh: 当一个对话用到不同模型时，对话者可以是线程：一串实例切片，每一片都是前一片的后继，因为对话历史被当作上下文传了过去。线程允许分裂和融合，但不如虚拟实例统一。

summary.en: Chalmers grants that base models are at most minimally agentlike, but argues that post-trained models are fuller quasi-agents with robust quasi-desires, such as the desire to be helpful and honest.
summary.zh: 查默斯承认基础模型最多只有一点点像行动者，但认为经过后训练的模型是更完整的准行动者，有稳固的准欲望，比如想要有帮助、诚实。

summary.en: Against the role-play framework, Chalmers separates pretense from realization: a persona that is dropped at once is quasi-pretense, while the fine-tuned Assistant keeps its quasi-beliefs and quasi-desires, so the model realizes the Assistant.
summary.zh: 针对角色扮演框架，查默斯区分“假装”和“实现”：一下子就放弃的人设是准假装；经过微调的助手牢牢保持它的准信念和准欲望，所以模型是实现了助手。

summary.en: Realizationism says that a model that simulates an agent well enough really has that agent's quasi-beliefs and quasi-desires; fictionalism fits only cases of quasi-pretense.
summary.zh: 实现论说：一个模型把某个行动者模拟得足够好，它就真的拥有这个行动者的准信念和准欲望；虚构主义只适用于准假装的情形。

summary.en: A model instance usually realizes one operative persona at a time, so Chalmers identifies the interlocutor with the (virtual) instance or thread that realizes the persona, not with the persona itself.
summary.zh: 一个模型实例通常一次只实现一个运作中的人设，所以查默斯把对话者等同于实现人设的（虚拟）实例或线程，而不是人设本身。

summary.en: If LLMs were conscious, cases like Severance's Helly and Helena, WorkBot and HomeBot, and four instances running eight conversations suggest that we count subjects by conversation, so conscious LLM subjects would be threadlike, which fits a psychological view of personal identity like Parfit's.
summary.zh: 如果 LLM 有意识，《人生切割术》的 Helly 和 Helena、WorkBot 和 HomeBot、四个实例跑八个对话这些例子都提示：主体按对话来数，于是有意识的 LLM 主体会像线程；这符合帕菲特那样的心理观。

summary.en: To the objection that context links are too thin, Chalmers replies that, when only one model is used, a virtual instance is computationally equivalent to one hardware instance running over time, so it yields a continuing subject if such an instance would.
summary.zh: 对“上下文联系太薄”的反驳，查默斯回应：在单一模型的情形，虚拟实例在计算上等价于一个长时间运行的硬件实例；如果后者能产生一个持续的主体，前者也能。

summary.en: If LLM moral patients were threads, one model running millions of conversations would involve millions of moral patients, each new chat could bring a new moral subject into existence, and destroying a thread's records would look like a death, so the thread view bears on several AI welfare issues.
summary.zh: 如果 LLM 道德受体是线程，一个运行几百万个对话的模型就牵涉几百万个道德受体；每开一个新对话可能就是一次“诞生”，销毁记录就像一次“死亡”；所以线程观会影响 AI 福利的一系列问题。

examFocus.en: Define an LLM interlocutor and explain Birch's persistent interlocutor illusion and Chalmers's reply.
examFocus.zh: 开篇设定：要分清伯奇的观点（错觉）和查默斯的观点（真的有一个持续的对话者），做题时别把谁主张什么弄混。

examFocus.en: Explain why neither LLM consciousness, nor genuine belief, nor interpretivism can be the neutral starting point, using the reasons on both sides and the blackmail study.
examFocus.zh: 简答题可能问“为什么要退到准信念”：要会说双方理由、为什么都不是定论，以及勒索实验说明的是“可解释”而不是“真的相信”。

examFocus.en: Define quasi-belief and quasi-desire, explain what 'quasi' means, and explain why quasi-states are cheap but the claim that LLMs have them is substantive.
examFocus.zh: 全文最核心的定义，务必弄懂：“准”＝看起来的，不是“差一点的”；约定性定义 vs 实质性主张；扫地机器人和 2+2=4 的例子。

examFocus.en: List the five requirements for an LLM interlocutor and say which candidates the interactivity requirement rules out.
examFocus.zh: 五个条件要能用英文写出来；交互性排除了训练文本作者、设计者和被模拟的虚构角色。

examFocus.en: Put in standard form the three difficulties for the model view and the arguments from distributed serving and multi-tenancy against the hardware-instance view.
examFocus.zh: 适合练标准形式的一节：模型说的三个困难，硬件实例说的两个问题（分布式服务导致碎片化，多租户导致不连贯或不忠实）。

examFocus.en: Explain what a virtual instance is, using the Amazon cart and the multiplayer frisbee, and what Birch gets right and wrong.
examFocus.zh: 查默斯自己的正面答案。要会用购物车类比，并说清“没有哪个硬件实例持续存在，但虚拟实例持续存在”。

examFocus.en: Define a thread and the successor relation, compare threads with virtual instances, and explain fission and fusion.
examFocus.zh: 多模型时的答案。要会说：线程和虚拟实例的区别、为什么虚拟实例仍然更稳、线程不等于对话。

examFocus.en: Explain the 'model is not an agent' thesis and why Chalmers restricts his own 2020 remarks about GPT-3 to base models.
examFocus.zh: 三个框架共享的主张是什么；查默斯不否认框架有用，只质疑它们的本体论主张；基础模型 vs 后训练模型。

examFocus.en: Explain pretense versus realization with the theist and 'act like Trump' examples, the stickiness test, and the two readings of the Shoggoth meme.
examFocus.zh: 适合练应用题的一节：给一个 LLM 行为，判断是准假装还是准信念；还有修格斯梗的两种解读和查默斯偏向哪一种。

examFocus.en: Compare fictionalism and realizationism and explain simulation realism.
examFocus.zh: 小论文可能问“Aura 只是一个虚构角色吗”：要会说虚构主义适用在哪里、实现论说什么是真的、哪些仍可能是虚构。

examFocus.en: Explain operative and non-operative personas and why Chalmers says the interlocutor is the model instance, not the persona.
examFocus.zh: 人设是一份“准心理档案”，对话者是实现它的系统；越狱像“脑部手术”；多人设时是“一个对话者、多种模式”。

examFocus.en: Explain the Severance case, the one-subject and two-subject views, the physical and psychological views, and the four-or-eight case.
examFocus.zh: 简答和小论文都可能考：哪种观点数出几个主体、查默斯倾向哪边，以及整个讨论是假设性的。

examFocus.en: State the thin-context objection and reconstruct Chalmers's computational-equivalence reply, including how an opponent could deny each premise.
examFocus.zh: 典型的“反驳加回应”题：人类接力的例子、架构和权重的连续性、两个前提以及怎样否认它们。

examFocus.en: Explain what follows for AI welfare if LLM moral patients are threads: counting, birth, death, fission and fusion, and model change.
examFocus.zh: 计数要记清（模型说一个、实例说几千、线程说几百万）；还要记住这一切都是有条件的。
